findings.evidence: Preface rule (PDF p.23): 'Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3.' Violating instances: PDF p.48 'derived in Ch 4 §4.3 and carried in Table 4-2' and 'the ~64 GB runtime/workspace reserve that Ch 7 §7.1 states as an assumption'; PDF p.74 'Ch 7 §7.4 re-derives the per-token value for other geometries'; PDF p.125 'Chapter 14 §14.4 (Acceptance test for a quantized deployment)'; PDF p.142 'resident KV slots (Ch 4 §4.3, §4.6)'; PDF p.156 '6 hosts, Ch 4 §4.3)'. Correct bare forms also occur, e.g. PDF p.62 '(§4.3)' and PDF p.84 '(see §4.3 and Table 4-1)'.
findings.issue: Recurrence of a house-rule violation: six references repeat the chapter number after the chapter name, exactly the form the Preface forbids. Under the book's own parsing rule ('§ N.M means Chapter N, Section M' plus 'the section number may stand alone'), 'Ch 7 §7.4' resolves to Chapter 7, Section 7.4 (= §7.7.4), which does not exist, instead of the intended §7.4; the same mis-resolution applies to 'Ch 4 §4.3' (should be Ch 4 §3), 'Ch 7 §7.1' and 'Chapter 14 §14.4'.
findings.fix_instruction: Sweep all six instances and drop the chapter digit from the section specifier: 'Ch 4 §4.3' → 'Ch 4 § 3' (PDF pp.48, 142, 156), 'Ch 7 §7.1' → 'Ch 7 § 1' (p.48), 'Ch 7 §7.4' → 'Ch 7 § 4' (p.74), 'Chapter 14 §14.4' → 'Chapter 14 § 4' (p.125); leave already-correct forms such as 'Ch 8 §3.4' (PDF p.32) unchanged.

findings.evidence: Page 46 (§2.1.2): "[1P][FACT] (Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff.)" and "[1P][DERIVED] (Wan2.2 TI2V-5B configuration, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff.)"
findings.issue: A DERIVED label is attached to a configuration statement (model/card geometry, i.e. what the source states) rather than to an arithmetic result computed from stated inputs. Elsewhere in the book (Preface, p. xvi–xvii; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 Note 1) DERIVED is defined strictly as "computed by arithmetic from stated inputs" and FACT as "directly stated by the source". Page 75 (§3.6.2) labels the same Wan2.2 counts "[1P][FACT]" ("at about 27B total and about 14B active parameters as published"). The same source, same kind of content, therefore carries FACT on p. 75 and DERIVED on p. 46 — an internal contradiction in the evidence taxonomy.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the p. 46 second label from [1P][DERIVED] to [1P][FACT] (the configuration is a source-stated fact, matching §3.6.2's treatment of the same Wan2.2 counts), or reword the sentence so the label applies to an actual arithmetic result.

findings.page: PDF p.58 (book p.34, Ch.2 §2.5); second instance PDF p.56 (book p.32, §2.3)
findings.chapter: Ch. 2 — What Actually Happens During Inference
findings.evidence: Instance 1 (PDF p.58, book p.34): "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [2°: industry rule of thumb][HYPOTHESIS][UNMEASURED] — not measured or cited here." Instance 2 (PDF p.56, book p.32): "the [2°] industry range is 30–40%, and the 35% point is the book's chosen planning value." The book's own Axis-1 definition: "[2°] — reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark" (PDF p.20, Preface) and "[2°] reputable second-hand (textbook, survey, independent benchmark)" (Table 4-2 Note 1, PDF p.104). Corroborating internal tension: Ch 2 §2.7 (PDF p.60, book p.36) lists the same quantity (sustained HBM bandwidth for weight-read kernels) as "a hypothesis to be measured on real hardware before it is cited" — i.e., the book itself says the figure is not yet citable, yet §2.5 assigns it second-hand provenance.
findings.issue: Provenance-label mismatch by the book's own taxonomy (recurrence: 2 instances in Ch. 2). [2°] is defined as a nameable reputable second-hand source (textbook/survey/independent benchmark), but both usages attach [2°] to uncited industry folklore — and the first sentence explicitly concedes "not measured or cited here", which contradicts the provenance claim the tag makes. The epistemic-axis tags ([HYPOTHESIS], [UNMEASURED]) are correct; the Axis-1 [2°] tag is the defect. No numeric harm results (the values are flagged unmeasured and used only as sensitivity context), so P3.
findings.fix_instruction: For each instance, either cite the specific second-hand source (named survey or independent benchmark) so [2°] resolves per its definition, or relabel as [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] (keeping [UNMEASURED] on Axis 3) or [UNRESOLVED], since no citable second-hand source currently exists; align §2.5 with §2.7's treatment of the same quantity.
